Review of spec pose-closeout-review-policy-by-cost-benefit, implemented by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic). The ADR `.pose/adr/2026-11-12-closeout-review-policy-by-cost-and-benefit.md` is Accepted; judge the implementation against it and the spec, not the decision itself.

Mechanism. Review policy schema 5 adds `milestone_review_required` / `roadmap_review_required` (`never|when-justified|always`), validated in `parseReviewPolicy` via `validateCloseoutReviewPolicyKeys` (closeout_review_policy.go). One evaluator `evaluateCloseoutReview` (closeout-review@1): canonical members `xref:<project>/spec:<slug>` (aliases, verified redirects, federated resolver, unknown = diagnostic, never zero) and ADR associations (closeout_adr_associations.go: roadmap `adrs:`, ADR `roadmaps:`, local Markdown links both ways; malformed/missing/unreadable = unknown). `closeoutReviewGate` is the single entry for readers: receipt first, roadmap done before adoption = legacy (nil decision), else evaluate + `protectCloseoutDecision` (baseline policy at the change set base when the scope changes the review contract); exemption only when not required AND no review recorded on the scope (`scopeReviewRecorded`, unreadable counts as recorded). Consumers: `reviewCheck` (review_closeout.go, Required=false + ApprovalOrigin), `proportionalReviewVerification` (review_bundle.go; under adoption the legacy singleton inheritance and `unreviewed_milestones` are skipped), `getCloseoutState` (CloseRequired, receipt, terminal only with receipt, new diagnostics), `ReachedMilestones`/`RoadmapsReachedBy`/`roadmapReachedApartFrom` (roadmaps.go), `milestoneReachedObligations`, `ReviewPlan.CloseoutReview` (out of the digest), doctor (`CloseoutReviewsOwed`), setup and `pose adopt` (capability_catalog.go `closeoutReviewPolicyCatalogEntry`, `SetCloseoutReviewPolicy`; refs/transfer adopt/retire no longer lower schema 5). CLI close (cli/review_closeout.go `closeoutReceiptPreflight`, `publishCloseoutReceipt`): milestone and roadmap close publish an immutable receipt (closeout_receipt.go, ExpectAbsent publish, strict parse); a done roadmap without receipt is completed by a new close. `milestoneMember` now maps `spec:<slug>` to its slug (was `spec:spec:<slug>` in closeout state). Existing tests changed on purpose: catalog lists, schema after adopt (fresh install is now schema 5), progressive_review fixtures that force schema 2, and the previous-release compatibility test (a fresh install is refused by v7.4.0 by its schema, by ADR design; an updated legacy instance stays readable).

Please do an exhaustive sweep in this round and report ALL findings together, classified blocker vs follow-up. Inventory every entry point that answers "is this aggregate scope approved / closed / reached" (CLI close, closeout-check, review-check, review verify, review-plan, attention/obligations, reached, nextCloses, roadmap check, MCP closeout state, federated acceptance, doctor) and check each one reads the same gate, cannot launder a recorded rejection under `never`, cannot let `always` be weakened by inheritance or `unreviewed_milestones`, and never treats an unknown member/association as an exemption. Also check: receipts are never overwritten nor fabricated for history; `pose update` never adopts; no schema-5 downgrade path; the recovery path for a roadmap done without receipt cannot close a scope whose review is required and unapproved.

Known pre-existing state: `pose check --strict` reports 19 delivery-contract errors of other specs (runtime worktree, common-domain handoff, governance performance, bounded graph caches), identical line by line on the base commit 956153f1; they are follow-up F4, not this spec.

Required tools: run `pose artifact-check --spec pose-closeout-review-policy-by-cost-benefit --strict` and `pose surface-check --spec pose-closeout-review-policy-by-cost-benefit --strict`; declare each `passed` only after running it (evidence `command:<the command>`, rationale quoting its result). The surface-check disposition must cite both an `integration:` and a `reachability:` sealed evidence id. Cite sealed `unit:`/`integration:` ids for criteria, never `SD-…` structural facts or requirement ids. Send each shell command alone in its own call (no pipes, `;`, `&&`, redirects). `validate` of a component with registered checks is `passed` with the sealed run's evidence; `review-check` and `closeout-check` are `deferred`. New findings have bare ids (F1, F2 …); follow-ups carry `action`, `owner`, `review_by`; only low-severity risks may be accepted.

Dispositions of round 1, all fixed in code with tests unless noted (see the spec's "### Review"): R1-F1 `mandatoryHumanReview` in `currentCloseoutDecision`; R1-F2 a close with a receipt requires `state.Terminal`; R1-F3 recovery via `CloseoutRecoveryDecision` (exempt only when known, unprotected exemption impossible, no review on file) and refusal when a recorded review is not approved; R1-F4 `closeoutReceiptStands` (same canonical members, else error) and parse refuses `always` with required=false; R1-F5 close intent (`PublishCloseoutIntent`/`ClearCloseoutIntent`, `closeoutScopeHistorical` requires no receipt and no intent); R1-F6 gate before enabled/cutoff in `reviewCheck`; R1-F7 receipt-bound proof in `federatedSourceProof`; R1-F8 preflight and publication share `CurrentCloseoutDecision`; R1-F9 exemption refuses any non-lifecycle blocker, publication re-verifies decision, members, ADRs and state in the protected region (before the status for a roadmap, because the index lags after it); R1-F10 transferred members go through the resolver to their final identity, unknown without one; R1-F11 associated ADRs are read and validated; R1-F12 `ReviewPlan` returns the gate error; R1-F13 `roadmapGate` normalizes `spec:<slug>`; R1-F14 the gate requires `Known` and `reviewCheck` blocks unknown; R1-F15 doctor requires a fresh approval via `ReviewCheck`.
